learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the fascinating world of the human mind, how we behave, and how psychology evolved from philosophy into a modern science!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Psychology is defined as a science which studies mental processes, experiences, and behavior in different contexts.
The brain is a physical organ with a specific location, whereas the mind is an abstract entity shaped by our experiences and interactions. You can see a brain on an X-ray, but not a mind!

Psychology grew through various schools of thought: Structuralism (studying structure of mind), Functionalism (how mind helps us adapt), Behaviorism (focusing only on observable behavior), and Psychoanalysis (unconscious desires).

Psychology has many specialized fields like Cognitive Psychology (thinking/memory), Developmental Psychology (lifespan changes), Clinical Psychology (mental health), and Social Psychology (how others influence us).
Psychology is not just for clinics; it helps solve daily problems, improves communication, helps in education, and promotes personal well-being.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The Introspection Game
fun_activity.instructions: Early psychologists used 'introspection' (looking inward). Sit quietly for 2 minutes and try to describe your exact thoughts, physical sensations, and emotions right now. It's harder than it sounds to be completely objective!

exam_tips: 📌 Always define psychology using the three key terms: Mental Processes, Experiences, and Behavior.
📌 Know the founders of the major schools of thought: Wilhelm Wundt (Structuralism), William James (Functionalism), John B. Watson (Behaviorism).
📌 Differentiate clearly between a Clinical Psychologist (uses therapy) and a Psychiatrist (has a medical degree and can prescribe drugs).
quick_recap: ⭐ The first psychology laboratory was established in 1879 by Wilhelm Wundt in Leipzig, Germany.
⭐ Behavior can be overt (outwardly observable) or covert (internal mental processes).
⭐ Modern psychology is a natural science as well as a social science.
